title: In search of novel ductile superconductors
abstract: We performed a first-principles high-throughput screening of the mechanical properties of phonon-mediated superconductors selected from the recent experimentally synthesized superconducting materials database PRX Energy 4, 033012 (2025). We developed the workflows that combine first-principles calculations of elastic constants and generalized stacking fault energies to assess the ductility of superconducting candidates. Starting from the 250 materials identified with promising superconducting critical temperatures, we computed their elastic tensors to evaluate bulk and shear moduli, Pugh's ratio, and Pettifor's ratio from first principles. To further characterize their plastic deformation behavior, we calculated the stacking fault energy and surface energy for selected materials and slip directions, allowing the estimation of Rice's ratio and ductility indicators. We found that several new materials simultaneously exhibit high-T$_c$ and ductility including HfPd$_2$Al, TiRuSb, and ZrNi$_2$Ga with predicted isotropic T$_c$= 6.80K, 12.88K, and 8.23K, respectively. This work offers a quantitative mapping of mechanical performance across a wide range of superconductors and provides a reference to identify new mechanically promising superconductors.
summary: This work systematically screens potential superconducting materials by calculating their fundamental mechanical properties using first-principles DFT. By developing quantitative indicators based on elastic constants and stacking fault energies, the authors successfully pinpointed several new compounds that are predicted to be both highly superconducting and mechanically ductile.
main_problem: To assess the practical viability of novel superconducting materials by correlating their high critical temperatures ($T_c$) with their mechanical properties, specifically ductility.
main_result: The study identified several new candidates ($	ext{HfPd}_2	ext{Al}$, $	ext{TiRuSb}$, and $	ext{ZrNi}_2	ext{Ga}$) that simultaneously exhibit high $T_c$ and predicted structural ductility.
method: First-principles calculations using DFT were employed in a high-throughput screening workflow to compute elastic constants, stacking fault energies, and various mechanical ratios.
model_or_system: The research focuses on phonon-mediated superconductors selected from an experimentally synthesized database. The analysis involves modeling the bulk mechanical response (elastic tensors) and plastic deformation behavior of crystalline solids.
key_observables: Pugh’s ratio ($r_{	ext{Pugh}}$), Pettifor’s ratio ($r_{	ext{Pett}}$), Rice’s ratio, superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), bulk/shear moduli, and generalized stacking fault energies ($\gamma$).
important_parameters: The ductility criteria are linked to $r_{	ext{Pugh}} \approx 0.57$ and the comparison between calculated ratios and their average values.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on DFT calculations, with initial discrepancies noted between Born expansion and finite-displacement methods, leading to a preference for the latter for high-throughput screening.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares $r_{	ext{Pugh}}$ and $r_{	ext{Pett}}$ from different calculation methods; Figure 2 correlates these mechanical ratios against $	ext{T}_{	ext{iso}c}$ and crystal structure family.
paper_structure: The paper develops a workflow to calculate elastic tensors for 250 candidates, establishes diagnostic indicators ($r_{	ext{Pugh}}, r_{	ext{Pett}}$), refines these indicators by incorporating plasticity (Rice's ratio into $c^*$), and finally identifies specific materials meeting both high-$T_c$ and ductile criteria.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter mechanics, the rigorous application of first-principles methods to link electronic/superconducting properties ($T_c$) with macroscopic mechanical stability (ductility) represents a powerful multi-physics approach relevant to designing novel quantum materials.
